cards.text: The Israelites are about to get their portions of the land of Canaan. Handing them out are Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, Israel's leader, and the heads of the families of the tribes. Moving day, friend, but for a whole NATION.

cards.question: True or false: The land for the nine and a half tribes is assigned by lot, as the LORD commanded through Moses.

cards.text: Why nine and a half? Moses already gave the other two and a half tribes their land east of the Jordan, and Joseph's descendants became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim.

cards.question: One tribe is different. The Levites get no portion of the land, except ___ to live in, along with ___ for their flocks and herds.

cards.text: So the Israelites divide the land, just as the LORD commanded Moses. Then the sons of Judah come to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite speaks up: "You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea about you and me."

cards.question: Caleb was forty years old when Moses sent him from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land. Caleb says he brought Moses back an ___ report.
True or false: Caleb says he joined the other spies in making the hearts of the people melt with fear.

cards.text: Caleb remained loyal to the LORD his God. Then he says that on that day, Moses swore to him that the land his feet had touched would be an inheritance for him and his children forever.

cards.question: Why does Moses promise Caleb that land?

answers.text: Because Caleb wholly followed the LORD
Because Caleb was the oldest spy
Because Caleb led the other spies

cards.text: Caleb says that, as the LORD promised, He has kept him alive forty-five years since then, while Israel wandered in the wilderness. Forty-five YEARS holding onto a promise, and I stare at a twelve-minute oven timer like it owes me money.

cards.question: Caleb was forty when Moses sent him to spy. Add those forty-five years. How old is Caleb now?
True or false: At eighty-five, Caleb says he's still as strong as he was the day Moses sent him out.

cards.text: Just as strong for war, for going out and for coming in. Friend, a few years of stamping and MY edges went blurry, and this man is eighty-five and still ready for battle.
Then Caleb makes his ask: "Now therefore give me this hill country that the LORD promised me on that day." And he reminds Joshua that Joshua heard back then who was living up there.

cards.question: Who does Caleb say lives in the hill country he's asking Joshua for?
The Anakim in that hill country have great and fortified cities. How does Caleb say he might drive them out?
Joshua blesses Caleb son of Jephunneh and gives him ___ as his inheritance.

cards.text: Hebron belongs to Caleb to this day, because he wholly followed the LORD, the God of Israel. And get this: Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, after a man named Arba.

cards.question: Who was Arba, the man Kiriath-arba was named after?

answers.text: The greatest man among the Anakim
A king who ruled from Gilgal
A priest who served with Eleazar

cards.text: Then the land had rest from war. Caleb held onto one promise for forty-five years, and here it is, friend, with his name on it.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "Now therefore give me this hill country that the LORD promised me on that day.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Moses first appears here and is never introduced. No card says who he is, and card 3 mentions him again with no introduction.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Because Caleb wholly followed the LORD', uses the Bible's wording ('wholly followed'). The two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ('the oldest spy', 'led the other spies'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke says 'a few years of stamping and MY edges went blurry'. His backstory says he wore down after years of baking with the Millers, as cutters arrived 'over the years'. 'A few years' changes how long that took.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This is a who question, so its wrong answers should be real Bible details. 'A king who ruled from Gilgal' isn't a real detail from anywhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Cards 10 and 13 have real laughs. Card 1's 'Moving day, friend, but for a whole NATION' reads like a pleasant dad line. Story cards 3, 5, 8, 14 and 18 are flat retellings, even though some moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, like an 85-year-old asking for the hill country full of Anakim and fortified cities.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
